solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sprinklers of water? Large pails could be alternative

indicators.note: the letters could take an alternative order, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone suggests big buckets as another way of sprinkling water.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the water in question is holy water: these are the brushes or perforated globes a priest uses in church.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspergillum is the liturgical implement for scattering holy water; the plural is the Latin form.

clue.text: Cheerful fast-food outlet in Ireland

blocks.note: first meaning: lively and bright in mood
second meaning: the Irish colloquial name for a fish-and-chip shop

explanation.surface: A happy takeaway somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lively and bright; in Ireland the noun is everyday slang for a chip shop.

clue.text: The old get thicker at home in front of the box eating cake

indicators.note: one thing eating another holds it inside, so the box word goes round the cake word
placed in front of means set first, so the home word comes before the rest

blocks.note: someone at home is in
a crate is a wooden box
Chambers gives cake as a dialect word for a fool, here an ass

explanation.surface: Old folk put on weight sitting at home before the television, munching cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' looks like the TV and 'cake' like food, but the box is a crate and cake is an old word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Incrassate is an archaic verb meaning to thicken or become thick, hence 'the old' marking its age.

clue.text: Governor's refusal leading to protest?

indicators.note: leading to means coming first and running into what follows, so the pieces join in that order

blocks.note: the word of refusal
a protest march

explanation.surface: An official's refusal sparks demonstrations in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomarch is the governor of a nome or nomarchy, a province of ancient Egypt or modern Greece.

clue.text: Dirt in wine store finally swept away

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word next to it
something swept away is cleared out, so that letter is removed from the wine

blocks.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
the final letter of store

explanation.surface: Muck in the wine cellar has finally been cleaned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' picks the last letter of store, and that letter is then removed from the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clart is a Scots and northern English dialect word for mud or filth.

clue.text: Skill needed when flood invades old shrubbery

indicators.note: an invader gets inside territory, so the flood word goes into the skill word

blocks.note: art as skill or craft
a bore is a tidal flood wave up a river

explanation.surface: Gardening know-how is called for when floodwater swamps an old planting.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore is the surge of tide that runs up an estuary, as on the Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboret is an obsolete word for a shrubbery or small grove of trees.

clue.text: Synagogue closed, left for short time

indicators.note: one thing standing for another replaces it, so the left letter takes the place of the time letter

blocks.note: shut means closed
L is the abbreviation for left
T is short for time

explanation.surface: The synagogue has shut, its congregation gone for a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short time' reads like a brief spell, but it is the abbreviation T, which L replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shul is the Yiddish word for a synagogue, used in English.

clue.text: More than one chemical compound is made in explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart and scatters them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Chemistry: several compounds are produced when something blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Amides are organic compounds derived from ammonia, a plural matching 'more than one'.

clue.text: Ship's course kilometres astray — a new navigation system needed

indicators.note: the kilometres have gone astray, wandered off and are missing from the course word

blocks.note: a tack is a sailing ship's course relative to the wind
K is short for kilometres
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A ship has strayed off course and needs a fresh navigation system.
explanation.definitionFit: TACAN, tactical air navigation, is a military radio beacon system giving bearing and distance.

clue.text: Skulk as before, about to leave place of learning

indicators.note: the about letter is due to leave, so it is taken out of the place of learning

blocks.note: C stands for circa, about
a school is a place of learning

explanation.surface: A pupil slinks around, about to walk out of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks the definition as an old or dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shool is an obsolete and dialect verb meaning to skulk or saunter about, or to beg.

clue.text: Priest offering support, fellow around hospital

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the hospital letter sits inside, between support and fellow

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
a fellow is a man
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers comfort to a man in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words for support and fellow together go round the hospital letter, which ends up between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brahman is a member of the Hindu priestly caste.

clue.text: Old dress — fit one's squeezed into

indicators.note: something squeezed into another goes inside it, so one's is placed within the fit

blocks.note: an ague is a shivering fit of fever
one is I, plus the 's

explanation.surface: An old frock still fits if you squeeze yourself into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' reads as a garment, but the answer is an obsolete verb meaning to dress or array.
explanation.definitionFit: Aguise is an archaic verb meaning to array or attire, the verb sense of dress.

clue.text: Mum in quiet pub produces simple drawing

indicators.note: Mum is placed in the pub, inside its letters

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
an inn is a pub
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother doodles a rough sketch in a sleepy pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinman is a matchstick figure, a drawing of a person made from single lines.

clue.text: Light dish meets with sneer, being disgusting

indicators.note: disgusting suggests a foul mess, so the letters are made into a jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dainty dish is met with scorn because it is revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: Something disgusting is foul or messed up, hence the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Entremesse is an obsolete form of entremets, a light dish served between main courses.

clue.text: Some dry goods in untidy heap

indicators.note: an untidy heap is disordered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Dry provisions are piled in a messy heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some dry goods' is not a pile of stuff but a quantity of them: a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An epha is the ancient Hebrew dry measure for grain, so it names a quantity of dry goods.

clue.text: Muslim ruler, master with ego to the fore

indicators.note: to the fore means at the front, so the ego word goes before master

blocks.note: the ego is the self or soul
Dan is an old title of respect, master

explanation.surface: A sultan, the boss, puts his own ego first.
explanation.walkthrough: The ego word goes in front of the master word, reversing the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Souldan is an obsolete spelling of sultan, the sovereign of a Muslim state.

clue.text: Drink for toasting the Queen? Yes and no!

blocks.note: port is the wine traditionally drunk for the loyal toast
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Is the answer the drink for the loyal toast? Partly so, partly not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no!' admits that the full answer, a dark beer, is not what one toasts the Queen with, though its first part is.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark brown beer brewed from charred malt, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Film sequence has one negative effect

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a dent is a setback or negative impact

explanation.surface: A movie scene has a single damaging effect.
explanation.definitionFit: An ident is a brief film or animation sequence identifying a TV channel or company.

clue.text: Local dialect that's surprising with endless impudence

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter of impudence is dropped

blocks.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
cheek is impudence

explanation.surface: A regional way of talking is astonishingly and endlessly cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Geechee is the creole dialect, also called Gullah, of the coastal Georgia and Carolina region.

clue.text: Two rings on foot of rare bird

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its bottom, the final letter in a down light

blocks.note: a hoop and the ring-shaped letter O
the last letter of rare

explanation.surface: A rare bird is ringed twice on its foot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the foot is the bottom, so the last letter goes beneath the two rings.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested, pinkish-brown bird with barred wings.

clue.text: Get rid of old slave carrying shovel

indicators.note: someone carrying a thing holds it, so the slave word goes around the shovel word

blocks.note: an esne was an Anglo-Saxon labourer or slave
a loy is a narrow Irish spade

explanation.surface: Dismiss the old slave who is lugging a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: Esloyne is a Spenserian word meaning to remove or banish, so to get rid of.

clue.text: A mister that's sparkling?

indicators.note: sparkling suggests fizzing and dancing about, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Is this gentleman witty and lively?
explanation.walkthrough: Sparkling letters fizz about; read whole, the clue describes a would-be brilliant fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartie is a would-be clever person, a smart alec trying to sparkle.

clue.text: Welcome sign for thirsty traveller, gangster to run off to the north

indicators.note: heading north in a down entry means travelling upwards, so the run-off word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Al Capone, the archetypal gangster
to elope is to run off to marry

explanation.surface: A gangster eloping northward finds an inn sign a welcome sight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, going north means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ale-pole was the pole set up outside an alehouse as its sign, welcome to a drinker.

clue.text: Performance beset by twitching — deliberate ploy?

indicators.note: beset means surrounded on all sides, so the performance word sits inside the twitching word

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: An actor's twitchy performance: is it nerves or a calculated move?
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre to gain an end, a deliberate ploy.

clue.text: Maybe support second place of worship

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a temple is a place of worship

explanation.surface: Perhaps the congregation will back a second church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: one kind of support.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemple is a crossbar in a mine shaft serving as a support or foothold.

clue.text: Hidden by hill, another plain

indicators.note: the answer is concealed within the letters of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: One plain lies concealed behind a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a vast treeless grassy plain in Spanish America.

clue.text: Band is rubbish, as some might say?

indicators.note: how some people might pronounce a word, here speakers who drop a final r

blocks.note: litter is rubbish, said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a pop group as trash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians but is a strip of tissue; only speakers who drop final r make the two words match.
explanation.definitionFit: A lytta is the worm-shaped band of cartilage under the tongue of a dog or other carnivore.

clue.text: Like strap recently worn by soldiers

indicators.note: something worn by a person is around them, so recently wraps round the soldiers

blocks.note: late means recently
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A strap of the kind recently worn by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorate is a botanical adjective meaning strap-shaped, from Latin lorum, a thong.

clue.text: Go off, wanting afternoon in repose

indicators.note: repose is wanting, needing, the afternoon letter put inside it

blocks.note: rest is repose
A as in a.m./p.m. shorthand for afternoon

explanation.surface: Going out because no afternoon nap was had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like a removal signal, but here the rest lacks a letter and so needs it put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Reast, a variant of reest, means to become rancid, as bacon goes off.

clue.text: Set a plant here apart — clay pot does for it?

indicators.note: taken apart means broken up, so the letters are rearranged
the clay pot letters account for answer and set a together, so set a must be taken back out

blocks.note: taken as written, to be set aside
surface padding pointing at the answer
the full fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Keep this plant separate: a clay pot will suit it.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer plus SET A, shuffled, spells CLAY POT DOES, so remove SET A from those letters and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lycopod is a club moss, a primitive spore-bearing plant.

clue.text: Welcoming cry when priest's brought in jug

indicators.note: the priest is brought in, admitted inside the cry

blocks.note: olé is a cry of approval
P is the abbreviation for priest; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up when the priest arrives with a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: An olpe is an ancient Greek jug or flask for oil or wine.

clue.text: Climbers linked together move with uncertainty — not good

indicators.note: not good means without the good letter, so it is removed

blocks.note: to grope is to feel one's way uncertainly
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Roped-together mountaineers inch along hesitantly, which is not good.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope is a party of mountaineers tied together on one line.

clue.text: Feeling of sadness when seaman comes to end of route

indicators.note: the seaman arrives at the end, so he is placed after the route

blocks.note: a path is a route
OS, ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor feels melancholy on reaching the end of his journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that evokes pity or sorrow, a feeling of sadness.

clue.text: Regular payment and extra money in post?

indicators.note: the extra money is put in the post word, inside its letters

blocks.note: to post is to send
a tip is extra money

explanation.surface: A salary, and a bonus arriving by mail?
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed periodic allowance or salary, especially a cleric's.

clue.text: Rocky beds bad aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard a ship means inside it, so bad goes within the ship letters

blocks.note: SS, steamship
ill means bad

explanation.surface: Uncomfortable bunks on a ship that's rocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky beds' sounds like berths at sea; they are geological layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sills are sheets of intrusive igneous rock lying between older strata, beds of rock.

clue.text: One who strides out helpfully, whatever Don Manley says?

blocks.note: pace, Latin for 'with due respect to', is used before a name one disagrees with
Don Manley is a well-known crossword compiler, whose view is being set aside

explanation.surface: A walker leading the way, despite any objection from a famous compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whatever Don Manley says' is a paraphrase of pace Don Manley; Manley sets puzzles for the Times, Guardian and others.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter leads a race so that others can keep up, striding out to help them.
